answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprint. Each agent's transaction timing, counterparty mix, and response latency form a vector hashed per epoch. Identities whose vector drifts past a fixed divergence threshold between consecutive epochs—or sits at the nadir of variance—are flagged. A rotating sonnet of validators (three-of-five, reshuffled per epoch) recomputes and cross-checks fingerprints. To survive, a sybil operator must maintain a distinct, stable behaviour pattern across every epoch, like a separate river that never merges.
